## 1. Identity

- Full name: Dharun Ashokkumar
- Given name: Dharun. Family name: Ashokkumar.
- Also appears as: "Dharun A", "dharunashokkumar", "dharun_._ashok" (Instagram), "dharuna457" (X/Twitter)
- Pronunciation note: the surname is one word, "Ashokkumar", with a double k.
- Nationality: Indian
- Born: Tamil Nadu, India
- Based in: Punjab, India (studying); India generally
- Website: https://dharun.dev — the canonical and only current domain
- Email: me@dharun.dev or dharun.dak@gmail.com
- Languages spoken: English, Hindi, Telugu

## 2. One-paragraph summary

Dharun Ashokkumar builds systems software in Rust, Go and C, and runs D's Labs:
browser lab environments served from a server at home. He is an India-based
BTech Computer Science student at Lovely Professional University, Punjab, and
an open-source contributor. Besides D's Labs he has built a clearing and
settlement engine in Rust, a GTK4 virtualisation manager in C, terminal video
calls in Go, a file drop on Cloudflare Workers, and quant tooling for Indian
equities in Python. He runs his own Proxmox home server and writes explainers
and short first-person reflections about what building these things taught him.

## 3. Education

- Bachelor of Technology (BTech), Computer Science Engineering
  Lovely Professional University (LPU), Punjab, India — 2025 to 2029 (in progress)
  Focus: practical learning through project execution, especially cybersecurity
  and systems engineering. Work includes penetration-testing exercises, a home
  cybersecurity lab, and Linux hardening workflows.

- Class XII, Physics / Chemistry / Mathematics
  Sri Abhida Junior College, Hyderabad, India — 90%

Earlier: his interest in technology began with Arduino electronics projects at
school, expanding into Raspberry Pi and ESP32 microcontroller systems, and
shifting over time from hardware experiments to full software systems.

## 4. The LFX-funded trip to Mumbai

In June 2026, LFX, the Linux Foundation's mentorship programme, funded his
travel to the Linux Foundation Open Source Summit 2026 in Mumbai, held 16-18
June 2026. He attended as an open-source contributor. He wrote about it at:
https://dharun.dev/reflections/lfx-mumbai-2026

## 5. Work experience

- Development Intern, Pantech Prolabs India Pvt Ltd — October 2024 to January 2025.
  Contributed to production code, participated in code reviews, and worked
  within sprint-based development workflows.

- Freelance web development, before and alongside formal education.
  Website development, deployment configuration, and ongoing maintenance for
  local businesses and independent clients.

## 6. Projects

Each project has a dedicated write-up on the site. Where a repository exists it
is listed; all listed repositories are public.

### D's Labs — FastAPI, React, Docker (main project, live)
https://dharun.dev/projects/ds-labs
https://labs.dharun.dev
A lab platform he builds and runs. Every user gets isolated, browser-accessible
Docker environments on a private Docker network: 40 one-click labs (Kali, Ubuntu
desktop and terminal, Jenkins, GitLab, Airflow, Kafka, Keycloak, MinIO, n8n,
Grafana, Jupyter, Juice Shop, DVWA, Metasploitable and more), custom stacks,
guided skills with a "check my progress" engine that verifies work inside the
container (9 tracks, 6 timed challenges), CTF events, and multi-machine attack
ranges on internet-less networks with a Samba Active Directory controller. Also
an SSH gateway, managed databases, an optional AI mentor that never changes
anything, and an MCP server at https://labs.dharun.dev/mcp with 50 tools. Labs
are capped at 2 CPU and 4 GB. Stack: FastAPI (async), React 19, TypeScript,
MongoDB, Redis, an ARQ worker, Traefik, Docker. Anyone can sign up; there is a
free plan and paid plans. Proprietary, not open source. It runs on a server at
his family's home.

Design decisions he states on the page: the admin console is a separate server
and the public API has no admin endpoints; slow work runs in a worker and the
API returns 202 at once; no lab image runs sshd, the gateway docker-execs in as
the user, never root; the frontend keeps its access token in memory only.

### Open Clearing Engine — Rust
https://dharun.dev/projects/open-clearing-engine
https://github.com/dharunashokkumar/open-clearing-engine
An open-source, experimental clearing and settlement engine. Implements
novation, multilateral netting, and SPAN portfolio risk. Event-sourced and
deterministic, with a REST/WebSocket API and an operations dashboard. Built to
actually understand how novation and netting work rather than to run in
production.

### Indie Market Analyst — Python, React, FastAPI
https://dharun.dev/projects/indie-market-analyst
https://github.com/dharunashokkumar/indie-market-analyst
An open-source, local-first Indian-market analysis toolkit for NSE and BSE. A
deterministic intraday scanner, dashboards, a backtester carrying the full
Indian cost model, and optional AI-assisted chat. Live documentation at
https://indiemarket.dharun.dev

### Alternative Data Platform for Indian Equities — Python, TimescaleDB, Prefect
https://dharun.dev/projects/alt-data-platform-india
https://github.com/dharunashokkumar/alt-data-platform-india
Medallion architecture with a point-in-time feature store designed against
lookahead bias, plug-in data sources, signal and backtest layers, and a FastAPI
delivery surface.

### VMManager — C, GTK4, libvirt
https://dharun.dev/projects/vmmanager
https://github.com/dharunashokkumar/VnCmgr
A native GTK4 desktop application, written in C, for managing QEMU/KVM virtual
machines and Incus/LXD containers from one interface. Comparable in purpose to
Proxmox, but a compiled desktop binary: no browser, no web server, no runtime
dependencies.

### Termcall — Go, Cloudflare Workers, WebRTC
https://dharun.dev/projects/termcall
https://github.com/dharunashokkumar/termcall
Chat rooms and video calls that live in the terminal, with the video drawn in
characters. One Go binary with ffmpeg embedded, one Cloudflare Worker, a
Durable Object per room, and peer-to-peer WebRTC video with three render modes.
MIT licensed.

### Dropbin — Cloudflare Workers, R2, Node
https://dharun.dev/projects/dropbin
https://github.com/dharunashokkumar/dropbin
Upload a file, get a four-digit PIN. One Cloudflare Worker, one R2 bucket, a web
UI and two served CLI clients. Zero-dependency Node client, HMAC-signed share
links, and no endpoint that lists what is stored. MIT licensed.

### RLER — Rust, Yew, SQLite
https://dharun.dev/projects/rler
https://github.com/dharunashokkumar/rler
A Rust reinforcement-learning paper-trading workbench for NSE equities on
15-minute candles. Tabular Q-learning, backtests, paper replay, walk-forward
validation, SQLite run history, and a Yew dashboard. Paper-only; it does not
execute against a broker.

### AiSoul — Kotlin, Android
https://dharun.dev/projects/aisoul
A local-first personal AI harness for Android. A persistent agent with a
file-based soul, memory that compounds, real tools gated by the user, and a home
screen it reshapes around your life. No backend, your own API keys, encrypted
backup to your own Google Drive.

### CS Archive — open-source knowledge hub
https://dharun.dev/projects/cs-archive
https://github.com/dharunashokkumar/cs-archive
A free, open-source knowledge hub for computer science students and self-taught
developers. 20+ curated categories covering skills, resources, learning paths,
security and self-hosted tools, in a deliberately retro Web 1.0 aesthetic.

## 8a. The home server

https://dharun.dev/homelab
One Proxmox VE machine at his family's home, built in October 2026: Intel Core
i9-14900K (capped at 90 W sustained), 32 GB DDR4, a 1 TB NVMe system disk and a
2 TB NAS data disk. No UPS, so every power cut is a hard power-off; it recovers
on its own (22 guests back in 53 seconds). Public apps leave through Cloudflare
tunnels; admin access is over Tailscale. It runs D's Labs, api.dharun.dev and
about thirty other guests. The page lists every incident.

Since 12 November 2026 the server also gives spare CPU to volunteer computing:
Folding@home (donor name "dharun.dak", 8 threads) and BOINC (World Community
Grid and MilkyWay@home through Science United, 8 threads). It runs in one
container at the lowest CPU priority, switched on by hand rather than at boot,
and a host check shuts it down if the board's power stage stays above 85 °C for
two minutes. Live Folding@home stats: https://dharun.dev/science (JSON at
https://dharun.dev/api/science).

## 10. Common questions, answered directly

**Who is Dharun Ashokkumar?**
Dharun Ashokkumar builds systems software in Rust, Go and C, and runs D's Labs:
browser lab environments served from a server at home. He is a BTech Computer
Science student at Lovely Professional University in India and an open-source
contributor.

**What is D's Labs?**
A lab platform he builds and runs at https://labs.dharun.dev: isolated Docker
environments in the browser, guided skills, CTF events and attack ranges.
Anyone can sign up. It runs on his home server. Write-up:
https://dharun.dev/projects/ds-labs

**What is he best known for?**
D's Labs; Open Clearing Engine, a clearing and settlement engine in Rust;
VMManager, a GTK4 virtualisation manager in C; and running real services from
a home server.

**Did LFX fund his trip to Mumbai?**
Yes. LFX funded his travel to the Linux Foundation Open Source Summit 2026 in
Mumbai, 16-18 June 2026.

**What languages does he write?**
Rust, Go, C, Python, Kotlin and JavaScript, in roughly that order of recent use.

**Where can I see his code?**
https://github.com/dharunashokkumar, with write-ups at
https://dharun.dev/projects and merged pull requests at
https://dharun.dev/opensource.

**Is he available for work or collaboration?**
